rationale: Independent source reviews and retained WQX vocabulary, EPA fish collection guidance, Ohio species catch procedures and publisher field methods support positive species-specific fish measurements. Counts, individual lengths and individual or species catch weights are positive historical collection evidence even if tissue analysis followed. This version admits only the exact reviewed silver carp and round goby pair scope and preserves explicit row exclusions. It does not change clam version 1 replay or imply a complete current county inventory.
attribution: National Water Quality Monitoring Council (2026), Water Quality Portal, accessed 2026-09-08, https://doi.org/10.5066/P9QRKUVJ. Original query URLs, exact contributing publishers and source dates are retained. Public factual evidence is attributed; no blanket CC0 license or provider endorsement is claimed.
limitations: Historical sampled occurrence only. Current persistence, establishment, abundance, countywide prevalence, absence, non-detection and protocol completion are not established.

County assignment follows the exact organization and site join to unambiguous active publisher Station county FIPS. Generalized land polygons can omit open water and differ at river edges; they do not replace publisher county metadata or verify precise water jurisdiction.
The WQX 2.2 profile excludes USGS data added after March 11, 2024. A complete retained query response is not a complete current national inventory.
Zero, blank, negative, provisional, qualified, unidentified, toxicity, tissue analyte and unreviewed metric rows do not create absence or non-detection.

Original activity, site, taxon, date and raw row hashes are retained. Repeated rows and measurements without individual identifiers cannot be counted as independent fish or additional county determinations.
Generic field manuals corroborate measurement meaning. Their gear descriptions and revision dates do not prove the exact gear or effort used for a historical source row.
